No state facilities ban and operating public-accommodation protections mitigate the national baseline, but are not shown to override it. The assessment’s relative low-risk label is not a visitor protection; local custody practice is unknown.

Statewide protections and hate-crime coverage, plus no documented adult-targeting rule, improve on the national baseline. School bathroom restrictions and sports policies create narrower exposure; reversal is unverified, and national document and custody risks remain.
